meaning: 다정 (多晶, Dajeong) joins 다 (多, da), "abundant," with 정 (晶, jeong), "crystal-clear." Above all, it sounds just like 다정하다, "warm-hearted, affectionate," so that tender meaning is right there in the name. Soft and endearing, sound and sense are one — an affectionate, lovable name.

meaning: 강민 (强旻, Gangmin) pairs 강 (强, gang), "strong," with 민 (旻, min), "the wide sky." It pictures someone both strong and broad-minded. Clear and bracing, 강민 balances the sturdy 강 with 민, one of Korea's most loved syllables (as in Jimin and 하민, Hamin). Strength and gentleness in easy balance — a modern, well-rounded name.
surname_desc: Jeong (鄭) is Korea's fifth most common surname at about 4.3%. Its major clans (Dongnae, Yeonil) produced renowned scholars and statesmen throughout the Goryeo and Joseon dynasties.

short: Someone clever and ever at peace
meaning: 리안 (悧安, Rian) joins 리 (悧, ri), "clever and bright," with 안 (安, an), "peaceful and tranquil." It's a name meaning someone clever and ever at peace. Gender-neutral, it matches the English "Liam/Rian," so it travels effortlessly. Cleverness and peace give a modern, international impression.
surname_desc: Park (朴) is Korea's third most common surname at about 8.4%. Uniquely native to Korea, it descends from Bak Hyeokgeose, the legendary founding king of the Silla Kingdom.

short: Someone toward whom good origins come
meaning: 래원 (來源, Raewon) joins 래 (來, rae), "to come, to arrive," with 원 (源, won), "source, origin." It's a boy's name meaning someone toward whom good origins come. The 원 syllable, as in 지원 (Jiwon) and 재원 (Jaewon), symbolizes source and preeminence. With a soft ending, it gives a refined, thoughtful impression.
surname_desc: Lee (李) is Korea's second most common surname at about 14.7% of the population. Its most famous lineage, the Jeonju Lee clan, founded the Joseon Dynasty and ruled Korea for over 500 years.

meaning: 주안 (珠安, Juan) joins 주 (珠, ju), "pearl, jewel," with 안 (安, an), "peaceful and tranquil." It pictures someone precious and at peace. Soft and neat, it recalls the phrase "주 안에서" (in the Lord), giving it a faith-tinged ring, and matches the Spanish "Juan." Preciousness and peace meet in a gentle name.
surname_desc: Cha (車) is Korea's 38th most common surname at about 0.4%. The Yeonan Cha clan is its principal lineage; the character means 'chariot' — a name with a strong, dynamic sound.

meaning: 하람 (Ha-ram) is a native Korean name — the native Korean word for "heaven's gift." It carries no Chinese characters; the meaning lives right in the sound. Balanced in sound, one syllable open and one closed
surname_desc: Jang (張) is Korea's 9th most common surname at about 1.0%. The Indong Jang clan is the largest line, and the name has long been associated with scholars and military officials of the Goryeo and Joseon courts.

meaning: 철민 (哲旻, Cheolmin) joins brightness with sky, holding the hope of a mind clear and vast, someone whose wisdom might stretch as wide and open as the heavens above. It carries the quiet wish that they grow luminous in thought, unbounded in spirit. Spoken aloud, Cheolmin is crisp yet gentle, its consonants clean, its vowels open and easy on the breath. Abroad, it settles comfortably near Chenglei, familiar in rhythm, so the sound travels well between two worlds without losing its bright, sky-wide meaning.
surname_desc: Jeong (鄭) is Korea's fifth most common surname at about 4.3%. Its major clans (Dongnae, Yeonil) produced renowned scholars and statesmen throughout the Goryeo and Joseon dynasties.

short: Someone upright as an at peace
meaning: 정안 (正安, Jeongan) joins uprightness with peace, carrying the quiet hope that someone will walk through life honest and unbending, yet always settled and calm within. It's a name that wishes for integrity without harshness, steadiness without struggle. Spoken aloud, Jeongan flows softly, its open vowels giving it a gentle, grounded sound, crisp at the start and easy on the ear. Abroad, it settles comfortably near Dequan, familiar enough to greet the world without losing its quiet Korean warmth.
surname_desc: Seo (徐) is Korea's 13th most common surname at about 1.5%. The Dalseong and Icheon Seo clans produced distinguished scholars, including famed Joseon-era prime ministers.
